actualEvidenceRead.inference: The retained diagnostic directly locates missing continuations before the original timeout despite native completion and active/current admission. A returned optional-call site is not evidence a callback was invoked.

reviewFindings: Pending resolve/reject JSValues are retained in one optional pair; takeCallbacks marks settled and detaches the pair once under the delivery lock.
The detached local pair remains strongly retained while both delivery and session locks are released; callback invocation/final JSValue release occurs outside both locks.

The session keeps only weak delivery entries. Its cancel snapshots live deliveries, clears the registry under its lock, unlocks, then cancels pairs; no strong session-to-delivery ownership cycle is added.
finish does not unregister when merely queued. Cancellation can release pending continuations while the serial callback queue is blocked.
Registration rejection and guarded-JSValue construction failure both clear the pair; deinit removes any weak entry.
Settlement removes the registry entry before invoking JS; reentrant completion/cancellation cannot invoke the same pair twice or reacquire a held delivery lock.
Existing isActive/current-identity checks, rejection strings and async callback queue remain; no synthetic result, quota increase, timeout increase or suppression was introduced.
Network32 total/8concurrent and native data-query/cancellation8 quotas are unchanged. The new weak lifetime registry does not consume those quota slots.
All pre-existing query-cancellation, running-state and execution-guard code after the session is byte-identical.
Fetch and HTTP test files recover exact uninstrumented prediagnostic bytes; no DEBUG logger/reader is carried into the repair.
limitations: Actual Swift compilation, original HTTP transport, existing two GC/lifetime controls and full603 must execute on the corrected source.
The code review preserves existing active/current check race semantics; it does not claim universal cancellation or context-release behavior beyond the native tests.
The diagnostic proves this lost-continuation failure path; it does not establish that every possible HTTP timeout has this cause.
